sources: **State mid-term report** for the third cycle
meta.headline: **Partial implementation (B)** is the dominant outcome, and Greece gives a detailed National Report: marriage equality (Law 5089/2024, **A**), bans on conversion therapy and non-consensual intersex surgery, repeal of simple defamation, a second National Action Plan against Racism and Intolerance (2026), the 2025 EU-aligned domestic-violence law with stalking and cyber-harassment offences, pay-transparency legislation (2026), a National Guardianship System for unaccompanied minors (2024), a National Strategy on Disability 2024-2030, new prison alternatives and a National Climate Law. **No relevant action (C)** persists on treaty ratification (ICRMW, OP-ICESCR, OP-CRC-IC), the rights of the Turkish Muslim minority, the protection of human rights defenders, and investigation of pushbacks. There are clear regressions or rejections (**E**): in July 2025 Greece suspended the registration of asylum applications of people arriving by sea and provided for returns without registration, the Human Rights Committee remains gravely concerned about pushbacks, and Greece restates that it recognises only a religious minority in Thrace.

themes.theme: Ratification of & accession to international instruments

blocks.summary: Ratify outstanding instruments
blocks.rationale: The Committees recommend ratification of ICRMW, OP-ICESCR, OP-CRC-IC and the Domestic Workers Convention; Greece reports only the 2025 ratification of the Protocol to ILO Convention 29.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 5 — Greece: "Greece ratified in 2025 the Protocol to ILO Convention 29"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 2 — Committee on the Rights of the Child; Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "recommended that Greece ratify the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on a communications procedure"

recommendations.text: Ratify the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families (Albania) (Bangladesh) (Burkina Faso) (Côte d’Ivoire) (Libya) (Rwanda); Consider ratifying the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of their Families (Philippines) (Timor-Leste); Proceed with the ratification of the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families (Togo); Consider the possibility of acceding to the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families (Algeria); Become a party to the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families

Ratify the Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (Albania) (Belgium) (Cyprus) (Portugal) (Slovenia) (South Africa); Consider ratifying the Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (Senegal); Proceed with the ratification of the Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (Togo); Sign and ratify the Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights

Ratify the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on a communications procedure (Côte d’Ivoire) (Cyprus) (Czechia) (Ireland) (Maldives) (South Africa) (Ukraine); Consider ratifying the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on a communications procedure (Chile) (Slovakia); Promote the prompt ratification of the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on a communications procedure

themes.theme: Cooperation & Follow up with Treaty Bodies

blocks.summary: Open, merit-based selection of treaty-body candidates
blocks.rationale: Greece's mid-term report states that it has consistently nominated highly qualified candidates; no open, merit-based selection process is described.

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Adopt an open, merit-based process when selecting national candidates for United Nations treaty body elections

themes.theme: National Human Rights Action Plans (or specific areas) / implementation plans

blocks.summary: Implement national action plans
blocks.rationale: The second National Action Plan against Racism and Intolerance was adopted after an evaluation of the 2020-2023 plan, which found fragmented implementation; the unaccompanied-minor relocation scheme relocated 1,368 minors.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 9 — Greece: "Drawing on an evaluation of the previous 2020–2023 Plan, which identified fragmented implementation, weak inter-agency coordination and overreliance on project-based funding"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 56 — Greece: "1,368 minors of various nationalities were relocated to twelve EU Member States"

recommendations.text: Take effective action in implementing the measures indicated in the national action plan on the rights of persons with disabilities, the national action plan against racism and intolerance and the national action plan on the rights of the child
Implement the national action plan against racism and intolerance (2020–2023) to address hate crimes and hate speech directed against members of vulnerable groups
Continue with the implementation of the voluntary relocation plan for accompanied or unaccompanied migrant children suffering from serious illnesses or other vulnerabilities

blocks.summary: Include migrants in the national recovery and resilience plan
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Ensure that all migrants are included in the national recovery and resilience plan

blocks.summary: Strengthen non-discrimination policies and protection of minorities and LGBTIQ+ persons
blocks.rationale: Greece enacted marriage equality (Law 5089/2024), banned conversion therapy (Law 4931/2022) and non-consensual interventions on intersex minors (Law 4958/2022), adopted a National LGBTIQ+ Equality Strategy 2021-2025 and extended disciplinary sanctions for discrimination; discrimination, hate speech and weak implementation persist.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 15 — Greece: "Law 5089/2024 on civil marriage equality represents a historic milestone, extending the right to marriage to same-sex couples"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 21 — Greece: "Law 5225/2025 amended the Civil Servants' Code to extend an existing disciplinary offense"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 29 — JS5: "LGBTIQ+ individuals in Greece continued to experience discrimination, harassment, and an alarming escalation in hate-motivated violence"

recommendations.text: Continue taking affirmative action to eliminate discrimination against persons in situations of vulnerability and historically discriminated against
Take effective measures to prevent, combat and punish racist hate speech and hate crimes
Revisit policies and measures to prevent and counter hate speech and violence, especially against migrants and refugees, in compliance with its international obligations
Strengthen efforts to eradicate stereotypes and discrimination against migrants and refugees
Strengthen the penalties for violence targeting members of national, racial, ethnic and religious minority groups, women and gender non-conforming persons, acts of antisemitism and other hate crimes
Take measures to ensure that those belonging to ethnic, religious or linguistic minorities are effectively protected against any form of discrimination
Continue to strengthen public policies against discrimination in all its forms, to protect vulnerable minorities
Strengthen measures to combat all forms of racial discrimination, including in the employment sector
Continue to strengthen efforts to ensure that all crimes committed with a discriminatory motive are fully and effectively investigated
Take effective measures to combat all manifestations of intolerance, as well as rising Islamophobia
Continue to develop policies to fight hate speech crimes, including those against LGBTQI persons

blocks.summary: National strategy for Roma social inclusion
blocks.rationale: The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021-2030 is being implemented with a Roma Forum; the Council of Europe Commissioner calls for faster implementation and better monitoring.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 23 — Greece: "The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021–2030"

recommendations.text: Step up efforts to eradicate stereotypes and discrimination against migrants, refugees and Roma

Continue the work to safeguard full respect for the human rights of, and non-discrimination of, the Roma population in Greece, in line with its international obligations, and in doing so ratify and effectively implement the Framework Convention for the Protection of National Minorities
Take further steps to end discrimination against minority groups, including the Roma population, and meaningfully integrate Roma children within the education system

blocks.summary: Replace the judicial gender-change process with an administrative one
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation; JS5 requests that psychiatric evaluation for minors be abolished.

recommendations.text: Replace the judicial process concerning gender change by an administrative procedure, through a unilateral declaration in the appropriate registry, in accordance with the recommendations of the Greek National Commission for Human Rights

blocks.summary: Ratify Protocol 12 to the European Convention
blocks.rationale: ELEN recommends ratification of Protocol 12; none is reported.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 3 — ELEN: "recommended to ratify Protocol 12 of the European Convention on Human Rights"

recommendations.text: Adopt the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (European Convention on Human Rights) definition of hate speech crimes, and investigate, prosecute and condemn racist violence crimes and hate speech crimes against LGBTI+ persons

blocks.summary: Combat racism, hate speech and hate crime
blocks.rationale: Greece adopted a second National Action Plan against Racism and Intolerance (February 2026), created a Community-Oriented Policing Directorate with a Department for Combating Racism (Law 5187/2025) and extended the media regulator's remit to online platforms; CERD found implementation of the previous plan low and calls for stronger enforcement of article 82A and victim support.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 9 — Greece: "adopted in February 2026 the second National Action Plan against Racism and Intolerance"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 12 — Greece: "Law 5187/2025 established the Community-Oriented Policing Directorate as a permanent institutional structure"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 16 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination: "expressed concern about the low level of implementation of the National Action Plan against Racism and Intolerance, of 2020–2023"

recommendations.text: Strengthen access to justice and to assistance services for victims of racist violence, in particular within the framework of the mandate of the National Council against Racism and Intolerance
Strengthen efforts in combating racism, and protect the rights of all migrants, particularly women and children
Provide the necessary training to law enforcement officials, investigate racism or hate crimes, and hold those found responsible to account
Combating racial violence, especially against immigrants and refugees
Take steps to effectively prevent and combat hate speech and racist discrimination
Step up efforts to respond better to racist or xenophobic acts, including by training law enforcement personnel and magistrates in this regard
Continue the progress made in combating racism, racial discrimination and xenophobia

Take steps to further prevent, combat and punish racist hate speech in the media and hate crimes, provide training on hate crimes to law enforcement officials and the judiciary, and improve access to justice and access to services supporting victims of racist violence
Pursue its efforts to combat racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance
Set an effective mechanism to combat racially motivated action, including racist violence targeting migrants, as well as stereotypes and discrimination against them
Undertake an intensive national public awareness-raising campaign aimed at combating racial discrimination
Strengthen measures to address hate crimes, xenophobia, racism and racial discrimination and promote tolerance throughout the society
Enhance the capacities of law enforcement authorities entrusted with investigating hate and racial crimes and of services in support of victims of such crimes
Ensure adequate resourcing of law enforcement authorities entrusted with investigating hate and racial crimes

Adopt effective measures to prevent and punish hate speech and hate crimes and strengthen awareness campaigns to combat racist and xenophobic attitudes, including among law enforcement officials and judicial officials
Continue its efforts to combat racism, racial discrimination and xenophobia

Ensure that all forms of hate crime are investigated and prosecuted, with perpetrators held accountable, and ensure that appropriate training on hate crimes is provided to law enforcement officials and the judiciary
Continue improving the accessibility of services supporting victims of race-based violence

Develop the required administrative and legislative policies and measures to prevent the dissemination of ideas based on racial superiority, and provide effective, timely and equitable remedies to victims of racism, hate speech and hate crimes
Continue efforts to ban organizations that promote hate speech and racism, especially those directed against minorities and immigrants

blocks.summary: National strategy for Roma social inclusion
blocks.rationale: The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021-2030 is being implemented with a Roma Forum; the Council of Europe Commissioner calls for faster implementation and better monitoring.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 23 — Greece: "The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021–2030"

recommendations.text: Continue strengthening measures to combat intolerance and racist and xenophobic violence, particularly against refugees, migrants and members of the Roma community

Continue to strengthen awareness-raising measures on racist and xenophobic violence against migrants, refugees and members of the Roma community, as well as improving access to justice and support services for victims of this kind of violence
End human rights violations resulting from racist hatred and xenophobia, especially against refugees, migrants and Roma and other minorities

blocks.summary: Business and human rights legislation and national action plan
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Take and report on concrete policy measures to establish legislation that addresses the involvement of corporations in conflict-affected areas, including situations of foreign occupation, to prevent all violations

blocks.summary: National action plan on business and human rights
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Develop a national action plan in line with the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, with the aim of promoting respect for human rights in the context of business activities

blocks.summary: Climate action and participation
blocks.rationale: Greece adopted a National Climate Law (2022) with 55% and 80% reduction targets for 2030 and 2040, a National Adaptation Strategy and public online consultation of environmental legislation.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 107 — Greece: "Greece implements its National Climate Law (Law 4936/2022), setting emissions reduction targets of -55% by 2030 and -80% by 2040"

recommendations.text: Ensure the meaningful participation of women, children, persons with disabilities and local communities in the development and implementation of climate change and disaster risk reduction frameworks
Take concrete and sustainable measures to combat the negative effects of climate change

blocks.summary: Investigate excessive use of force and train law enforcement
blocks.rationale: Greece reinforced the disciplinary framework in 2024 (removal of officers in serious cases), weekly referral of cases to the Ombudsman and large-scale police training (27,130 officers since 2019); the Human Rights Committee remains gravely concerned about excessive and deadly force.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 69 — Greece: "The 2024 reform of the disciplinary legislative framework reinforced these guarantees by providing for the removal from active service of uniformed officers involved in serious criminal or disciplinary offenses"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 20 — Human Rights Committee: "expressed grave concern about the use of excessive and deadly force by the police and other law enforcement officials"

recommendations.text: Investigate reports of arbitrary conduct and allegations of unjustified violence by law enforcement authorities
Eradicate police violence and excessive use of force by law enforcement officials against peaceful protesters, including the use of tear gas against migrants and asylum seekers

Thoroughly investigate reported cases of excessive use of force by law enforcement officers, review crowd-control procedures applied in the context of demonstrations and provide training to all law enforcement officers on the use of force

blocks.summary: Investigate allegations of pushbacks and ill-treatment of migrants
blocks.rationale: Greece reports a three-tier complaints system, but the Human Rights Committee requests that the independence and impartiality of monitoring mechanisms be affirmed and investigations be effective.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 50 — Greece: "every allegation of illtreatment, including alleged pushbacks, is investigated at internal and/or EU level"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "affirm the independence and impartiality of the monitoring mechanisms involved in investigating violations of the human rights of migrants and asylumseekers at borders"

recommendations.text: Train law enforcement and border agents on human rights, and monitor, investigate and punish abuses in the use of public force

blocks.summary: Operational autonomy and resources of the national preventive mechanism
blocks.rationale: The Ombudsperson is the NPM under OPCAT and the national investigation mechanism; the Human Rights Committee requests that its resources be adequate.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 70 — Greece: "The Greek Ombudsman functions both as the National Preventive Mechanism (NPM) under OPCAT and as the National Investigation Mechanism"

recommendations.text: Ensure the operational autonomy of the national preventive mechanism against torture and provide it with the necessary financial and human resources
Ensure that the Greek Ombudsman, as the national preventive mechanism against torture, is provided with the necessary financial and personnel resources to function effectively

blocks.summary: Improve conditions of detention and reduce overcrowding
blocks.rationale: Law 4985/2022 created a judicial remedy on detention conditions, Law 5187/2025 and Law 5282/2026 introduced electronic monitoring and community service and a 2025-2030 action plan was adopted; the CPT still calls for urgent improvements and a strategy to reduce the prison population.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 66 — Greece: "Law 4985/2022 amended the Penitentiary Code to establish a judicial remedy enabling detainees to challenge their conditions of detention"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 67 — Greece: "Law 5282/2026 further introduced community service into the Penitentiary Code as an alternative to imprisonment"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 10 — European Committee for the Prevention of Torture: "recommended urgent improvements focusing on reducing cell occupancy, investing in maintenance, improving hygiene"

recommendations.text: Continue efforts to improve conditions of detention and develop rehabilitation programmes
Continue efforts to improve conditions of detention
Continue efforts to improve conditions of detention and reduce overcrowding in penitentiaries

Continue efforts to improve conditions of detention, alleviate the overcrowding of penitentiary institutions, reform the immigration detention system and ensure that migrants deprived of liberty are treated with both dignity and humanity
Continue efforts to improve conditions of detention and alleviate the overcrowding of penitentiary institutions, including through the application of non-custodial measures
Adopt and implement effective policies for ensuring that prison conditions meet international human rights standards
Reduce prison overcrowding and ensure that conditions in places of detention meet international standards
Bring its prison and detention conditions fully into line with international human rights norms and standards, including the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners
Continue its efforts to improve conditions of detention and alleviate the overcrowding of penitentiary institutions
Improve conditions in prisons and detention centres

blocks.summary: Ensure individual assessment of protection claims and stop collective returns
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: In July 2025 Greece suspended the registration of asylum applications from people arriving by sea and provided for their return without registration, a measure contrary to these recommendations; the Human Rights Committee remains gravely concerned about pushbacks.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 35 — Several submissions: "the submission of asylum applications by third-country nationals entering Greek territory by sea was suspended for a period of three months. The suspension allowed the return, without registration"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "remained gravely concerned about pushbacks of asylum-seekers, refugees and migrants at the country’s sea and land borders, in violation of the principle of non-refoulement"

recommendations.text: Ensure that refugee claims are subject to individual consideration to determine the international protection needs of applicants

Ensure that all asylum seekers have the opportunity to obtain an individual review of expulsion decisions, with automatic suspensive effect, and are protected against refoulement and collective referrals, given information regarding the violation of the principle of non-refoulement
Adopt measures to ensure that an individual assessment is carried out for each case of asylum, deportation or expulsion, with full respect for the principle of non-refoulement
Intensify efforts to assess asylum claims and stop collective deportations and returns of migrants
Strengthen legislative and policy response towards the full realization of the principle of non-refoulement and guarantee the rights of all migrants and asylum seekers

Protect persons entering Greece across land and sea borders, including by ensuring that border control operations both on land and at sea are conducted in accordance with international human rights law, including the principle of non-refoulement

blocks.summary: Investigate allegations of pushbacks and ill-treatment of migrants
blocks.rationale: Greece reports a three-tier complaints system, but the Human Rights Committee requests that the independence and impartiality of monitoring mechanisms be affirmed and investigations be effective.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 50 — Greece: "every allegation of illtreatment, including alleged pushbacks, is investigated at internal and/or EU level"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "affirm the independence and impartiality of the monitoring mechanisms involved in investigating violations of the human rights of migrants and asylumseekers at borders"

recommendations.text: Ensure swift and independent investigation and follow up on accusations relating to pushbacks of migrants, in accordance with its international obligations

Promptly and fully investigate reports of breaches of the principle of non-refoulement and allegations of summary forced returns of migrants at the European Union border between Greece and Turkey, including acts of violence or ill-treatment that may have occurred during such incidents

Set up an effective and independent mechanism to register complaints of refugees and migrants against the Greek authorities and investigate human rights violations reported by international organizations

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Ensure that allegations of forcible eviction of irregular migrants from its territory without due process are credibly investigated

Conduct thorough, transparent and credible investigations into reports of abuses against asylum seekers and migrants, including pushbacks at sea that endanger the lives of migrants, destruction of identity documents and the forcible deportationof asylum seekers holding valid residency credentials
Conduct a public enquiry regarding the cases concerning refugees and migrants, and ensure that those responsible are prosecuted

blocks.summary: Investigate pushbacks, ensure individual assessment and access to asylum
blocks.rationale: Greece describes a three-tier complaints system and a Fundamental Rights Officer, but the Human Rights Committee remains gravely concerned about pushbacks and questions the independence of the monitoring mechanisms; in July 2025 Greece suspended the registration of asylum applications of people arriving by sea.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 50 — Greece: "Greece has put in place a three-tier system to address complaints"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "remained gravely concerned about pushbacks of asylum-seekers, refugees and migrants at the country’s sea and land borders, in violation of the principle of non-refoulement"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 35 — Several submissions: "in July 2025, the submission of asylum applications by third-country nationals entering Greek territory by sea was suspended for a period of three months"

recommendations.text: Take effective measures to ensure the unacceptability in practice of confessions resulting from torture or ill-treatment
Conduct transparent investigations into allegations of excessive use of force by law enforcement officials
Continue to improve the criminal justice system and take measures to address arbitrary deprivation of liberty
Continue to comply with its obligations under international law in relation to the rights of migrants and refugees

blocks.summary: Protect refugees and migrants in accordance with international law
blocks.rationale: The Human Rights Committee remains gravely concerned about pushbacks and Greece suspended asylum registration in 2025.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "remained gravely concerned about pushbacks"

recommendations.text: Take the necessary steps to protect the human rights and dignity of refugees and put an end to systematic illegal pushbacks, in compliance with the relevant conventions
Ensure the protection of refugees and migrants in accordance with international standards, including ending the illegal practice of summary forced returns or collective expulsions

blocks.summary: Reception and living conditions of asylum seekers
blocks.rationale: Greece operates a modernised reception system (RIC, CCAC, Safe Areas, Hippocrates programme); the Human Rights Committee and CPT still request improved detention and reception conditions.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 46 — Greece: "Eight designated Safe Areas, supported by child protection personnel from NGOs and IOM"

recommendations.text: Ensure adequate reception and living conditions for asylum seekers, in line with the requirements of the European Convention on Human Rights and of European Union law, and continue to conduct investigations into allegations of illegal pushbacks of refugees
Implement immediate measures for asylum seekers, especially in the face of a probable increase in the flow of migrants and asylum seekers from Afghanistan

blocks.summary: Establish effective mechanisms to counter pushbacks
blocks.rationale: Greece denies that pushbacks are compatible with its procedures and points to a three-tier complaints system whose independence the Human Rights Committee questions.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 50 — Greece: "Allegations of pushbacks are not compatible with the well-established standard operating procedures of the Hellenic authorities"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "affirm the independence and impartiality of the monitoring mechanisms involved in investigating violations of the human rights of migrants and asylumseekers at borders"

recommendations.text: Establish effective mechanisms to counter pushbacks against migrants and refugees and ensure adherence to the principle of non-refoulement

blocks.summary: Do not detain children solely for immigration status
blocks.rationale: Greece reports safeguards for unaccompanied minors but the Human Rights Committee still calls for alternatives to detention.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "provide effective alternatives to the detention of migrants and reduce the length and practice of such detentions"

recommendations.text: Ensure that children are not detained solely because of their status under immigration law

themes.theme: Participation of women in political & public life

blocks.summary: Increase women's political and public participation and employment
blocks.rationale: A 40% candidate quota applies to all elections and the Gender Equality Observatory monitors it; women remain under 30% of elected bodies, and 2025 employment of women reached 62.3%.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 34 — Greece: "The legislative framework mandates a minimum gender quota of 40% of candidates in parliamentary, European Parliament, municipal and regional elections"

recommendations.text: Take further steps toward fostering greater participation of women in the political and public sphere

blocks.summary: Rights of the Turkish Muslim minority in Western Thrace
blocks.rationale: Greece maintains that only a religious Muslim minority exists and Law 4964/2022 keeps State involvement in the selection of Muftis; the Turkish community requests that its schools and associations be restored.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 25 — ABTTF: "law No. 4964/2022 should be repealed, and the functioning of the mufti offices should be determined by the community itself"

blocks.summary: Recognise the right to conscientious objection

evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 78 — Greece: "Under Law 5265/2026, applications are reviewed by a committee comprising three university professors, a State Legal Council member and one Armed Forces Officer"

blocks.summary: Freedom of religion or belief and conscientious objection
blocks.rationale: Law 5224/2025 regulates places of worship of all communities except the Orthodox Church, recognises Alevis and Law 5265/2026 revised the conscientious-objection procedure; alternative service remains longer than military service and the State remains involved in the selection of Muftis.
