Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 7 — JS6; JS7: "the punitive conditions of the alternatives to military service in Greece violated several human rights instruments"

recommendations.text: Continue efforts to guarantee the right to freedom of religion or belief of every member of the society

blocks.summary: Recognise conscientious objection and alternative service
blocks.rationale: Law 5265/2026 revised the review committee, but alternative service is longer than military service and civil society reports punitive conditions.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 78 — Greece: "Alternative service lasts 15 months, or, where reductions apply, 12, 9 or 5 months"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 7 — JS6; JS7: "the punitive conditions of the alternatives to military service in Greece violated several human rights instruments"

recommendations.text: Consider amending legislation in order for conscientious objectors to be able to perform alternative civilian service in their place of residence

themes.theme: Freedom of opinion and expression & access to information

blocks.summary: Decriminalise defamation and protect journalists
blocks.rationale: Law 5090/2024 repealed article 362 (simple defamation), a Memorandum of Understanding and Task Force on journalists' safety exist and Law 5253/2025 created a National Action Plan for the Safety of Journalists; OSCE-ODIHR requests that remaining criminal defamation and insult provisions be replaced by civil remedies.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 71 — Greece: "Law 5090/2024 repealed Article 362 of the Criminal Code, eliminating the offense of simple defamation"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 12 — OSCE-ODIHR: "criminal provisions for defamation and insult be replaced by proportional civil remedies"

recommendations.text: Ensure the freedom of expression and association of human rights defenders, volunteers and civil society organizations
Take the necessary measures to end threats and violence against journalists, in line with its commitments under international law

blocks.summary: Decriminalise defamation
blocks.rationale: Simple defamation (article 362) was repealed in 2024; OSCE-ODIHR requests that remaining criminal defamation and insult provisions be replaced by civil remedies.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 71 — Greece: "Law 5090/2024 repealed Article 362 of the Criminal Code, eliminating the offense of simple defamation"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 12 — OSCE-ODIHR: "criminal provisions for defamation and insult be replaced by proportional civil remedies"

recommendations.text: Decriminalize defamation

blocks.summary: Protect human rights defenders and humanitarian workers
blocks.rationale: Law 5275/2026 simplified NGO registration but the Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders finds the registration regime discriminatory and reports a hostile environment and criminalisation of search-and-rescue work.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 58 — Greece: "Law 5275/2026 limited the registration requirement to organizations receiving state or EU funding or operating within Ministry facilities"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 25 — Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders: "since 2019, human rights defenders and NGOs working in the field of migration had reported an increasingly hostile environment for their work"

recommendations.text: Ensure that human rights defenders and humanitarian workers and volunteers are protected against threats, harassment and intimidation, and that they are not prosecuted for engaging in humanitarian work, including maritime search and rescue activities
Redouble efforts to guarantee the protection of human rights defenders, including those who carry out humanitarian work with refugees and migrants
Ensure that all human rights defenders, journalists and humanitarian workers are allowed to exercise their work, in a safe and enabling environment

blocks.summary: Stop prosecuting and intimidating human rights defenders
blocks.rationale: The Special Rapporteur reports criminalisation of search-and-rescue work and a hostile environment; Greece states defenders remain fully protected.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 26 — Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders: "criminalization of search and rescue activities at sea under national legislation"

recommendations.text: Stop prosecuting, including criminally, human rights defenders who investigate cases of summary forced returns or collective expulsions
End the intimidation, threats and harassment suffered by human rights defenders, in particular when carrying out humanitarian work

blocks.summary: Facilitate the work of non-profit organisations
blocks.rationale: Law 5275/2026 limited the registration requirement and removed the review committee, although the Special Rapporteur finds the regime discriminatory.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 58 — Greece: "no registration fee is charged and the three-member committee review has been removed"

recommendations.text: Revisit policies with a view to facilitating the legitimate work of non-profit organizations and individuals working with migrants and refugees

themes.theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery

blocks.summary: Prevent and combat human trafficking
blocks.rationale: Greece amended article 323A, runs a National Referral Mechanism (327 victims identified within Greece in 2025), is updating its National Action Plan and strengthened labour inspections; victim identification, resources and a permanent National Rapporteur remain gaps.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 61 — Greece: "amendments to Article 323A of the Criminal Code, reflecting the full range of exploitation forms and introducing enhanced protections for minors"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 63 — Greece: "327 victims were identified as exploited within Greece"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 15 — TSA: "the Office of the National Rapporteur on Human Trafficking lacked sufficient means and remained headed by an interim rapporteur since 2021"

recommendations.text: Pursue efforts aiming to combat human trafficking, labour exploitation and migrants smuggling
Continue taking effective measures to prevent and combat trafficking in persons
Continue efforts in combating human trafficking and upholding the rights of victims in this regard
Strengthen procedures for the identification and referral of trafficking victims, especially in the migration context, and ensure victims’ access to all needed services
Continue promoting the effective implementation of the national action plan on human trafficking

Increase efforts to prevent and combat human trafficking, in particular by putting in place effective procedures to identify victims within vulnerable groups and refer them to the relevant services, and redouble efforts to investigate suspected cases of human trafficking

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Accelerate efforts to implement its 2019 national action plan to combat trafficking in human beings and continue to provide training on the new national referral mechanism to all front-line responders and relevant officials
Continue its efforts to combat human trafficking
Intensify its efforts to combat trafficking in human beings, with particular attention to the needs of victims.

Strengthen efforts to prevent, respond to and ensure the identification of child victims of trafficking and exploitation, including through the development of an appropriate protective legal and policy framework
Adopt appropriate measures to protect children who are victims of sexual abuse and/or exploitation and trafficking
Keep up its efforts to prevent and combat trafficking in human beings
Continue efforts to address and prevent trafficking in persons for forced labour, particularly in the agricultural industry, and strengthen a victim-centred approach
Intensify its efforts to prevent and combat trafficking in persons
Intensify efforts to combat human trafficking, particularly of migrants and asylum seekers

blocks.summary: Legal recognition of same-sex relationships and marriage
blocks.rationale: Law 5089/2024 extended civil marriage to same-sex couples and recognises same-sex parents of children born abroad through assisted reproduction.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 15 — Greece: "Law 5089/2024 on civil marriage equality represents a historic milestone, extending the right to marriage to same-sex couples"

recommendations.text: Consider taking steps towards the legal recognition of same-sex relationships, including marriage, and the possibility of adopting children
Pass and implement laws that recognize same-sex marriage and the possibility of adopting children

themes.theme: Labour rights and right to work

blocks.summary: Narrow the gender pay gap
blocks.rationale: Law 5316/2026 requires pay transparency and sanctions unjustified pay disparities over 5%; the gap stands at 13.4%.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 37 — Greece: "sanctioning enterprises with unjustified pay disparities exceeding 5%, to operationalize pay transparency"

recommendations.text: Implement concrete measures meant to eliminate the gender pay gap and increase women’s participation in entrepreneurship, as well as reducing women’s unemployment and underemployment
Implement concrete measures for the reduction of the gender pay gap
Continue working to eliminate obstacles that prevent the full participation of women in the labour market and the gender pay gap
Ensure full and equal participation of women in the labour force, and implement measures to close the gender pay gap
Take action to narrow the gender pay gap

blocks.summary: Eliminate the gender pay gap and labour discrimination
blocks.rationale: Law 5316/2026 transposed the EU pay-transparency directive and Law 5239/2025 requires workplace harassment policies; the unadjusted pay gap stands at 13.4%.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 37 — Greece: "By Law 5316/2026 presented by the Ministry of Labor and Social Security and adopted in July 2026, EU Directive 2023/970 was transposed"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 36 — Greece: "the unadjusted gender pay gap stood at 13.4%"

recommendations.text: Step up action to combat any manifestation of labour discrimination and economic exploitation of migrant workers
Adopt comprehensive policies for the protection of women and girls, with special emphasis on the full and equal participation of women in the workforce and on reducing the gender wage gap
Continue to strengthen measures implementing the legislation pertaining to gender discrimination in the workplace

blocks.summary: Independent living and inclusion of persons with disabilities
blocks.rationale: A Personal Assistant service assisted 1,100 people, 4,700 buildings received accessibility subsidies and more than 700 people moved to supported living.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 85 — Greece: "Law 4837/2021 established the Personal Assistant service for persons with disabilities"

recommendations.text: Take effective measures to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities, particularly women with disabilities, in the open labour market
Take effective measures to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities, particularly women with disabilities, in the open labour market

themes.theme: Right to an adequate standard of living

blocks.summary: Social assistance, housing and living conditions
blocks.rationale: Greece operates the Minimum Guaranteed Income programme, raised the minimum wage and launched a EUR 6.5 billion housing programme; conditions in pre-removal and reception facilities draw criticism.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 101 — Greece: "The Minimum Guaranteed Income program provides financial assistance to extremely poor households and homeless individuals"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 103 — Greece: "A comprehensive 6.5-billion-euro program encompasses a rent rebate scheme"

recommendations.text: Further mitigate the impact of the economic crisis and austerity measures on the social and economic rights of the most vulnerable groups of society, as previously recommended
Continue to promote sustainable development and strengthen the social protection system
Continue consolidating social assistance plans and programmes through effective and inclusive social policies envisaged in “Greece 2.0”, the national recovery and resilience plan
Ensure adequate living conditions and access to services for refugees, asylum seekers and irregular migrants in reception facilities, with particular attention to those in vulnerable situations

blocks.summary: Reception and living conditions of asylum seekers
blocks.rationale: Greece operates a modernised reception system (RIC, CCAC, Safe Areas, Hippocrates programme); the Human Rights Committee and CPT still request improved detention and reception conditions.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 46 — Greece: "Eight designated Safe Areas, supported by child protection personnel from NGOs and IOM"

recommendations.text: Ensure that migrant and asylum-seeking populations detained in pre-removal facilities or residing at the country’s six reception and identification centres have healthy living conditions and access to education for children and are screened for trafficking indicators
Redouble efforts to address the challenges of securing humanitarian assistance for migrants and asylum seekers, especially women and children

blocks.summary: National strategy for Roma social inclusion
blocks.rationale: The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021-2030 is being implemented with a Roma Forum; the Council of Europe Commissioner calls for faster implementation and better monitoring.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 23 — Greece: "The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021–2030"

recommendations.text: Continue giving continuity to the national strategy for Roma social inclusion, and the action plans in the areas of housing, health, employment and education

blocks.summary: Participation of refugee and asylum-seeking women
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Ensure the meaningful participation of refugee and asylum-seeking women in decision-making on matters affecting their lives in the camps, and monitor and review the health, safety and living conditions of refugees

themes.theme: Economic, social & cultural rights - general measures of implementation

blocks.summary: Protect rights of persons in vulnerable situations
blocks.rationale: A new Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs and a multi-billion housing programme advance protection.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 6 — Greece: "The new Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs integrates policies on human rights, gender equality, child rights and vulnerable groups"

recommendations.text: Continue promoting and protecting human rights, especially the rights of women, children and vulnerable groups
Better protect the rights of persons in vulnerable situations, including women, children and persons with disabilities

blocks.summary: Conclude the national strategy on social integration and poverty reduction
blocks.rationale: JS2 requests that the strategy be fully implemented and funded, which implies it exists.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 11 — JS2: "fully implement and adequately fund the National Strategy for Social Integration and Poverty Reduction"

recommendations.text: Conclude the national strategy for social integration and poverty reduction, launched in June 2021 to address root causes of poverty, and implement programmes that mitigate the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on employment and livelihoods to ensure that all children and other household members can live in dignity and have access to affordable public services

blocks.summary: National strategy for Roma social inclusion
blocks.rationale: The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021-2030 is being implemented with a Roma Forum; the Council of Europe Commissioner calls for faster implementation and better monitoring.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 23 — Greece: "The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021–2030"

recommendations.text: Undertake action to combat child poverty, taking into account the vulnerability of Roma children and unaccompanied migrant children

blocks.summary: Improve access to health services
blocks.rationale: Asylum seekers receive a provisional insurance and healthcare number, the Hippocrates programme screens new arrivals and Roma vaccination campaigns run; sanitation and mental-health policy gaps persist.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 104 — Greece: "Asylum seekers benefit from a Provisional Insurance and Healthcare Number"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 45 — Greece: "Since July 2024, IOM's and partners’ Hippocrates program has provided medical and psychosocial screening"

recommendations.text: Continue supporting efforts to enhance the comprehensive response to the COVID-19 pandemic
Seek to establish a long-term strategy that would include effective measures to guarantee even more efficient access to health services for people with disabilities
Continue to strengthen measures to contain the pandemic in reception centres for migrants and refugees
Improve access to health services for persons with disabilities, particularly in sexual and reproductive health services

blocks.summary: Sanitation and health in refugee camps
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no specific information on sanitation measures.

recommendations.text: Improve the situation of migrants, particularly by safeguarding the health conditions of children and persons belonging to vulnerable groups, in line with its international obligations
Take additional measures to improve sanitation within refugee camps

blocks.summary: Human-rights-based mental health policies
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Implement human rights-based mental health policies aligned with the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and provide community-based mental health services, with a view to eliminating stigma, discrimination and coercion in mental health

themes.theme: Persons with disabilities: protecting the integrity of the person

blocks.summary: End involuntary hospitalisation of persons with disabilities
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no specific information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Put an end to involuntary hospitalization and involuntary deprivation of liberty on the basis of a psychosocial disability

blocks.summary: Inclusive and equal access to education
blocks.rationale: Greece operates Reception Classes and School Annexes, Educational Priority Zones, unconditional enrolment of Roma children and a 2025-2030 violence-prevention strategy; the CRC and OSCE-ODIHR note continued exclusion of Roma and migrant children and the Turkish minority's schools are not restored.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 98 — Greece: "Dedicated structures, Reception School Annexes, after-hours Reception Units and Refugee Education Coordinators guarantee access to formal education for refugee and migrant children regardless of documentation status"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 26 — OSCE-ODIHR: "expressed concern about the alarming situation of Roma children being out of formal education"

recommendations.text: Develop a long-term strategy to ensure equal access and quality of education for child asylum seekers, refugees and migrants and other vulnerable children

Make further efforts to counter discrimination and intolerance against disadvantaged persons based on their ethnicity and religion, with a special focus on equal access to quality education for all children
Strengthen efforts by adopting a coherent strategy on an inclusive educational system with the allocation of additional funds for educational materials and individualized support for those in need
Develop a long-term educational strategy with identified funding gaps to fully integrate all refugee and migrant children and children with disabilities into public schools
Take steps to dismantle obstacles to effective access to education, with a view to improving school attendance rates among children in vulnerable situations
Take further steps to guarantee inclusive education of children with disabilities in the mainstream education system
Step up efforts to ensure optimal access to education for migrants and refugees
Intensify efforts to provide access to education for all, especially migrants and refugees, and increase the participation of women in political life
Take further steps to promote equal opportunities for marginal communities in education and employment
Adopt a coherent strategy to ensure universal access to education, especially with regard to students with special Educational needs
Continue to implement measures to eliminate obstacles to access to education for all children, including children with disabilities

blocks.summary: National strategy for Roma social inclusion
blocks.rationale: The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021-2030 is being implemented with a Roma Forum; the Council of Europe Commissioner calls for faster implementation and better monitoring.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 23 — Greece: "The National Strategy and Action Plan for Roma Social Inclusion 2021–2030"

recommendations.text: Increase efforts aimed at fully integrating refugee and migrant children, Roma children and children with disabilities into the education system
Develop a long-term educational strategy to fully integrate all refugee and migrant children, Roma children and children with disabilities into public schools

blocks.summary: Protect unaccompanied minors
blocks.rationale: Greece launched a National Guardianship System (January 2024, 8,189 children served), a National Emergency Response Mechanism and Safe Areas; 1,465 unaccompanied children were in the system in May 2026.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 55 — Greece: "On 1 January 2024, the National Guardianship System for Unaccompanied Minors was operationally launched"

recommendations.text: Ensure adequate access to education, in accordance with article 13 of the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, for migrant children and unaccompanied minors by implementing European Union directives requiring member States to integrate children into their national school systems within three months of their identification

blocks.summary: Alternative classes for religious education
blocks.rationale: Children may be exempted from religious education without authorization or verification of religion.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 97 — Greece: "Children may be exempted from religious education without authorization, verification of religion or any associated sanctions"

recommendations.text: Consider alternative classes for the religious education of non-Orthodox students in schools

blocks.summary: Allow the Turkish minority to run its own schools
blocks.rationale: The Turkish community reports closure of its primary schools and restrictions on school boards; no measure is reported.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 24 — ABTTF: "the temporary suspension and subsequent permanent closure of Turkish primary schools"

recommendations.text: Allow the Turkish Muslim minority to establish and run their own schools, in compliance with international treaties

blocks.summary: Combat domestic violence
blocks.rationale: Law 5172/2025 and the Panic Button app strengthened the domestic-violence framework.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 39 — Greece: "The "Panic Button" digital application"

recommendations.text: Pursue the efforts made in combating domestic violence
Continue strengthening the fight against domestic violence, including through awareness-raising campaigns

blocks.summary: Institutional and policy framework on gender equality
blocks.rationale: Law 4604/2019 and a new Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs frame gender equality, a National Action Plan 2026-2030 is being prepared and the Gender Equality Observatory collects data; CEDAW finds the laws of limited effectiveness.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 31 — Greece: "Law 4604/2019 on the Promotion of Substantive Gender Equality mandates horizontal gender mainstreaming"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 41 — Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "expressed concern about the limited effectiveness of the laws and policies to protect women’s rights"

recommendations.text: Strengthen support for women in vulnerable situations, especially for women belonging to minority groups, including access to adequate shelters and long-term support
Invest additional efforts in providing the necessary funds for the General Secretariat for Gender Equality in terms of human, financial and technical resources
Continue efforts to support gender equality, protect women’s rights, and prevent violence against women
Build upon the institutional framework stablished under Law No. 4604/2019 to drive substantive gender equality and the elimination of gender-based violence

Implement concrete measures to raise public awareness of women’s rights, including by offering training for judges, prosecutors, police officers, health-service providers and school staff, in order to fully ensure women’s rights in all areas of public life
Continue its efforts to promote gender equality and eliminate discrimination against women through the implementation of the national action plan on women, peace and security

blocks.summary: Strengthen the national human rights institution's work on women's rights
blocks.rationale: The GNCHR completed its first comprehensive Report on the Status of Women in Greece in 2024; CEDAW requests that its resources be increased.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 33 — Greece: "In 2024, the GNCHR completed its first comprehensive Report on the Status of Women in Greece"

recommendations.text: Intensify efforts by the Greek national human rights institution to put in place concrete action aimedat raising awareness and eliminating discrimination against women

blocks.summary: Adopt the national action plan on gender equality
blocks.rationale: The incoming National Action Plan 2026-2030 is being prepared with civil-society input.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 33 — Greece: "The incoming Plan 2026–2030, currently under preparation with civil society input"

recommendations.text: Seek prompt adoption and implementation of the national action plan on gender equality (2021–2025), and strengthen the monitoring of and compliance with its pillars

blocks.summary: Prevent and respond to violence against women
blocks.rationale: Law 5172/2025 transposed the EU directive and criminalised stalking and cyber harassment, the 'Panic Button' app and 63 Domestic Violence Police Offices operate and a network of 65 facilities exists; shelter capacity is insufficient and femicide is not defined in law.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 39 — Greece: "Law 5172/2025, transposing Directive (EU) 2024/1385, has reinforced the domestic violence protection framework"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 40 — Greece: "Operational Domestic Violence Police Offices have increased from 18 to 63"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 38 — Greece: "the Government acknowledges that shelter capacity is insufficient and is committed to expanding it"

recommendations.text: Investigate all acts of violence against women and girls, including domestic violence, and increase support for victims, in line with the Istanbul Convention
Continue fighting against violence targeted at women and girls, especially by prevention and public awareness campaigns
Ensure that combating gender-based violence remains a key priority
Ensure universal access to high-quality services and access to justice for victims and survivors of sexual and gender-based violence
Provide universal access to quality services and to justice for survivors of gender-based violence
Take the necessary measures to adopt a comprehensive approach to preventing and addressing violence against women in all its forms
Enhance measures to prevent and combat violence against women, and extend those measures to reach women migrants and refugees living in camps and temporary accommodation
Continue stepping up efforts to prevent gender-based violence against women, including domestic violence, and to promote women’s empowerment

blocks.summary: Implement the Istanbul Convention
blocks.rationale: Law 5172/2025 transposed EU standards; the GNCHR and CEDAW call for a legal definition of femicide and a gender-killings observatory.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 39 — Greece: "In its report, the GNCHR stressed that an official definition of femicide and a dedicated observatory on gender-related killings should be established"

recommendations.text: Ensure the full and effective implementation of the Council of Europe Convention on Preventing and Combating Violence against Women and Domestic Violence, by, inter alia, adopting the necessary secondary legislation and implementing decrees
Implement the Council of Europe Convention on Preventing and Combating Violence against Women and Domestic Violence

blocks.summary: Strengthen migration and minority protection frameworks
blocks.rationale: Greece consolidated its reception and asylum legal framework (Law 4939/2022, Law 5307/2026), a Fundamental Rights Officer and a National Strategy for the Protection of Vulnerable Persons (June 2026); monitoring bodies' independence and pushbacks remain contested.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 51 — Greece: "Law 4960/2022 established, within the Ministry of Migration and Asylum, the post of Fundamental Rights Officer"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 57 — Greece: "the GSVPIP adopted, after public consultation, the National Strategy for the Protection of Vulnerable Persons"

recommendations.text: Continue taking practical steps aimed at the development of the institutional and human rights infrastructure to better implement its human rights obligations
Continue strengthening plans and policies for the protection of minority rights
Fully and swiftly implement the integration policy for refugees and asylum seekers
Continue its efforts to effectively manage the mixed migration flows with full respect for rights of migrants

Ensure that the legislative and policy responses as well as operational practices responding to migration are consistent with international human rights and refugee law, in particular the principles of non-refoulement and non-penalization of irregular entries

blocks.summary: Protect unaccompanied minors
blocks.rationale: Greece launched a National Guardianship System (January 2024, 8,189 children served), a National Emergency Response Mechanism and Safe Areas; 1,465 unaccompanied children were in the system in May 2026.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 55 — Greece: "On 1 January 2024, the National Guardianship System for Unaccompanied Minors was operationally launched"

recommendations.text: Further sharpen policies to ensure respect for the human rights of asylum seekers and migrants, paying special attention to the protection of unaccompanied minors

blocks.summary: Protect refugees and migrants in accordance with international law
blocks.rationale: The Human Rights Committee remains gravely concerned about pushbacks and Greece suspended asylum registration in 2025.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "remained gravely concerned about pushbacks"

recommendations.text: Ensure that the necessary legal framework governing NGOs operating in Greece does not inhibit their capacity to contribute to the protection of refugees and migrants (Ireland).

blocks.summary: Protect the rights of women and children
blocks.rationale: Gender-equality and child-protection frameworks were strengthened.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 31 — Greece: "Within the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family Affairs, created in 2023, the General Secretariat for Equality and Human Rights remains the lead body"

recommendations.text: Continue to take measures to protect the rights of women and children, including by strengthening its existing legislation

blocks.summary: Deinstitutionalisation and guardianship
blocks.rationale: Greece is transitioning to family-based care (foster-care platform, semi-autonomous living units) and launched a National Guardianship System for unaccompanied minors in 2024; the CRC finds children over-institutionalised.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 90 — Greece: "Greece continues the transition to family-based models"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 46 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "expressed concern about the overinstitutionalization of children deprived of parental care"

recommendations.text: Reduce the institutionalization of children by significantly increasing the use of family- and community-based alternative care

blocks.summary: Review the guardianship system
blocks.rationale: The guardianship system was launched in 2024 and Law 5307/2026 transferred the appointment of guardians to the General Secretary.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 55 — Greece: "Law 5307/2026 transferred competence for the appointment of guardians from the Public Prosecutor to the General Secretary"

recommendations.text: Review the system of guardianship and its functionality in practice

themes.theme: Rights related to name, identity & nationality

blocks.summary: Birth registration for children of migrants and Roma
blocks.rationale: The Committee on the Rights of the Child recommends further facilitation of birth registration; no new measure is reported.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 60 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "further facilitate access to birth registration procedures and identity documentation, and to correction of birth certificates for Roma children and children of migrant parents, free of charge"

recommendations.text: Consider measures to enhance the accessibility of birth registration to children of parents with irregular migration status

blocks.summary: Recognise the ethnic identity of the Turkish Muslim minority
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: The National Report restates that Greece recognises only a religious minority, without reference to ethnic origin, which rejects the recommendation.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 25 — Greece: "Greece recognizes as a "minority" the religious Muslim Minority in Thrace, the status of which was established by the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne, on the basis of religion, without reference to the ethnic origin of its members"

recommendations.text: Take the necessary steps to recognize the ethnic identity of the Turkish Muslim minority in Western Thrace and comply without any further delay with the judgments of the European Court of Human Rights of 2008 regarding three minority associations which were banned because of the words “Turkish” and “minority” in their names

blocks.summary: Strengthen the asylum registration system
blocks.rationale: Civil society reports the online asylum platform requires detention of up to 25 days and suspended registration in 2025.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 40 — Several submissions: "the new online platform to apply for asylum, introduced in 2022, required a detention period of up to 25 days"

recommendations.text: Strengthen the registration system for asylum seekers, as well as referral mechanisms, and ensure that the merits of applications and admissibility procedures are assessed on a case-by-case basis

blocks.summary: Adequate resources for implementing child rights policies
blocks.rationale: The CRC recommends a dedicated budget for the National Action Plan on the Rights of the Child; none is reported.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 13 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "recommended that Greece equip the National Action Plan with time-bound and measurable goals and a dedicated budget for its implementation"

recommendations.text: Ensure adequate human and financial resources for thorough implementation of the national action plan on the rights of the child

blocks.summary: Promote child rights, child-centred budgeting and child poverty reduction
blocks.rationale: Law 4837/2021 defined child abuse and created a national recording system, a 2025-2030 violence-prevention strategy was adopted and family benefits exist; the CRC calls for time-bound goals and a dedicated budget for the National Action Plan.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 88 — Greece: "Law 4837/2021, which introduced statutory definitions of child abuse and established the National System for Recording and Monitoring relevant incidents"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/2), para. 13 — Committee on the Rights of the Child: "recommended that Greece equip the National Action Plan with time-bound and measurable goals and a dedicated budget for its implementation"

recommendations.text: Continue its efforts in combating child poverty, protect their rights to health and education and ensure that all children, including children from families with low socioeconomic status and children of migrants, receive support and enjoy all child rights
Develop a child-centred budgetary policy, in combination with child mainstreaming, in all sectors of public policy

Strengthen efforts to further promote the rights of the child, taking into account the adverse impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and the economic crisis, through the implementation of the national action plan on the rights of the child, which was adopted in 2021
Adopt and implement measures for the prevention and cessation of all violations of the rights of the child, including the rights of migrant children

blocks.summary: Protect unaccompanied minors
blocks.rationale: Greece launched a National Guardianship System (January 2024, 8,189 children served), a National Emergency Response Mechanism and Safe Areas; 1,465 unaccompanied children were in the system in May 2026.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 55 — Greece: "On 1 January 2024, the National Guardianship System for Unaccompanied Minors was operationally launched"

recommendations.text: Continue the efforts of the Ministry of Migration and Asylum to promote the social integration of unaccompanied minors residing in Greece
Improve the conditions of those unaccompanied minors who are still living in insecure circumstances

blocks.summary: Rights of the Turkish Muslim minority in Western Thrace
blocks.rationale: Greece maintains that only a religious Muslim minority exists and Law 4964/2022 keeps State involvement in the selection of Muftis; the Turkish community requests that its schools and associations be restored.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 25 — ABTTF: "law No. 4964/2022 should be repealed, and the functioning of the mufti offices should be determined by the community itself"

recommendations.text: Introduce the necessary conditions for the Turkish Muslim communities in Western Thrace and in the Dodecanese to self-govern their waqf properties

themes.theme: Persons with disabilities: definition, general principles

blocks.summary: Inclusion of persons with disabilities and harmonisation with the CRPD
blocks.rationale: Greece adopted a National Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2024-2030, created a National Accessibility Authority, reserved 12% of public recruitment, funded personal assistants and deinstitutionalisation (700 people moved).
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 83 — Greece: "National Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2024–2030 sets targets across accessibility, employment, education, health and independent living"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 86 — Greece: "Law 4765/2021 reserves 12% of annual public sector recruitment for individuals with a disability rate of at least 50%"

recommendations.text: Intensify action to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the open labour market and to guarantee inclusive education of children and students with disabilities
Harmonize the national legal and administrative framework on disability with the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Step up measures to ensure that persons with disabilities are not excluded in the distribution of welfare allowances

Continue consolidating the achievements made in promoting the rights, inclusion, equal opportunities and well-being of persons with disabilities within the framework of the national programmes implemented
Develop effective and required measures to ensure an adequate standard of living for persons with disabilities, including their sufficient access to comprehensive health-care services

blocks.summary: Accessibility of services for persons with disabilities
blocks.rationale: Law 5023/2023 appointed accessibility officers in all courts and extended legal aid; Law 4997/2022 subsidises accessibility upgrades and accessibility offices are required in universities by 2026.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 87 — Greece: "appointing accessibility officers in all courts, and granting direct legal aid irrespective of income"

recommendations.text: Continue progress in the implementation of the existing legal framework on accessibility standards for persons with disabilities
Ensure effective access for persons with disabilities to justice, legal services and legal aid, and work out a long-term strategy for access to comprehensive health-care services
Focus on improving access for people with disabilities to information, through accessible formats and sign language interpretation
Ensure that health care and judicial and educational services are accessible to and inclusive of persons with disabilities

blocks.summary: Review the guardianship system
blocks.rationale: The guardianship system was launched in 2024 and Law 5307/2026 transferred the appointment of guardians to the General Secretary.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 55 — Greece: "Law 5307/2026 transferred competence for the appointment of guardians from the Public Prosecutor to the General Secretary"

recommendations.text: Continue the cooperation with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and human rights organizations, as well as work on improving the legislative and law enforcement system in order to increase the effectiveness of the institution of guardianship of unaccompanied children

blocks.summary: Cooperate with UNHCR and support migrant inclusion
blocks.rationale: Greece cooperates with UNHCR, IOM and EUAA on reception and integration (HELIOS programme).
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/1), para. 59 — Greece: "The HELIOS program facilitates access to the labor market and delivers targeted interventions, including cultural mediation"

recommendations.text: Provide support for the inclusion of recent migrants in society and continue to cooperate with African and other nations to implement policies that ensure safe and orderly migration and protect the human rights of all people

blocks.summary: Equal enjoyment of culture and use of minority languages
blocks.rationale: The Turkish community of Western Thrace reports closure of its schools and curbs on its autonomy; no measure is reported.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/GRC/3), para. 24 — ABTTF: "the temporary suspension and subsequent permanent closure of Turkish primary schools"

recommendations.text: Guarantee in practice the equal and effective enjoyment of culture and use of language by all persons, including Albanians living in Greece

meta.caveat: The Human Rights Committee's follow-up procedure grades only the two to four “priority” recommendations it selected from this country's Concluding Observations (CoBs). The other CoBs are not graded.

paragraphs.title: Excessive use of force and ill-treatment
paragraphs.recommendation: The State party should ensure that all allegations of unauthorized and disproportionate use of force by law enforcement officials are thoroughly and promptly investigated by an independent authority, that the alleged perpetrators are prosecuted, that those found guilty are punished with sentences that are commensurate with the gravity of the offence, and that compensation is provided to the victims or their families. The State party should also ensure that the police receive appropriate professional training that includes full respect for human rights principles

limbs.eval: The Committee welcomes the designation of the Ombudsman as the national mechanism for the investigation of incidents of ill-treatment committed by law enforcement and detention facility agents. It requires additional information on: (a) the mandate and actions taken by the national mechanism for the investigation of incidents of ill-treatment committed by law enforcement and detention facility agents to investigate allegations of unauthorized and disproportionate use of force by such agents; and (b) whether the State party envisages rendering the Ombudsman’s recommendations binding

The Committee regrets the lack of information on concrete measures taken after the adoption of the concluding observations to ensure that all allegations of unauthorized and disproportionate use of force by law enforcement officials are thoroughly and promptly investigated by an independent authority. It therefore requires information on: (a) the measures taken to punish, as well as the sentences imposed on, law enforcement officials for misconduct, ill-treatment or disproportionate use of force, after the adoption of the Committee’s concluding observations; (b) the progress of investigations made into the cases of Thanasis Panayotopoulos, Yannis Bekos, Vasilis Loukas and similar ones; and (c) the number, regularity, duration and content of professional training for police officers and other law enforcement agents conducted after the Committee’s concluding observations. The Committee reiterates its recommendation

paragraphs.title: Unaccompanied minors
paragraphs.recommendation: The State party should ensure that the principle of the best interests of the child is given due consideration in all decisions concerning unaccompanied children, including by: (a) Ensuring that unaccompanied minors who enter the country in an irregular manner are not detained or are held in detention only as a measure of last resort and for the shortest period of time necessary; (b) Creating new reception facilities and increasing the number of detention spaces in existing structures, while ensuring adequate conditions for unaccompanied minors in those facilities, including their segregation from adults; (c) Pursuing its efforts to redesign the guardian assignment procedure to ensure that each unaccompanied child is provided with a legal guardian; (d) Ensuring that the age assessment procedure is based on safe and scientific methods, taking the children’s mental well-being into account and avoiding all risks of violating their physical integrity

limbs.eval: The Committee appreciates the information provided by the State party and the data provided on the custody of unaccompanied minors, however, it regrets that the detention may be extended to periods of time that can be considered excessive. In this regard, the Committee requires the State party to provide information on the measures taken to ensure that unaccompanied minors who enter the country in an irregular manner are not detained or are only held in detention as a measure of last resort and for the shortest period of time necessary. It also requires information on the number of current and previous unaccompanied minors in custody since 2015, the duration of their custody, the vulnerability assessments made, medical assessments undergone, facilities sent to and guarantees provided to ensure that they are informed of their legal status and entitlement to legal aid. The Committee notes the information provided by the State party on the involvement of doctors and psychologists in the age assessment procedure. However, it regrets reports indicating that the procedure is intrusive and inaccurate and that it is not thoroughly implemented in all cases, particularly with respect to individuals who illegally entered or reside on the mainland. The Committee therefore requires information on whether any steps have been taken to develop a standard protocol for the age assessment procedure, which is applicable to any individual whose age is questioned. The Committee reiterates its recommendation

The Committee welcomes the information provided, including the increase in the number of shelters from 17 to 41 and the addition of approximately 690 places to the pre-existing 420, as well as the information provided on the separation of unaccompanied minors from adults and the services and safe zones provided to them. The Committee requires information from the State party on the steps taken to continue its efforts in analysing the current needs and building new shelters with the aim of reducing the number of unaccompanied minors awaiting placement in shelters. The Committee welcomes the envisaged draft laws on guardianship and foster care, but regrets the lack of specific information on their content. The Committee requires information on: (a) how the aforementioned laws would enhance the protection of children deprived of parental care; (b) which guarantees are included in the special provisions for unaccompanied minors; and (c) what progress has been made in the draft bills’ legislative process and implementation

paragraphs.title: Expulsion of asylum seekers and undocumented immigrants
paragraphs.recommendation: The State party should ensure that all persons seeking international protection have access to fair and personalized assessment procedures, protection against refoulement without discrimination and an independent mechanism with the authority to suspend negative decisions. The State party is encouraged, in consultation with its international and regional partners and neighbours, to allow migrants wishing to enter its territory to have access to safe entry points where their asylum claims can be evaluated. The State party should also take all the measures necessary to ensure that informal returns do not occur and that immigrants are not subjected to illtreatment during their deportation and expulsion or while in pre-removal centres. The State party should also ensure that ill-treatment of refugees and migrants is effectively reported, undertake, as a matter of priority, prompt, effective and independent investigations into all claims of irregular returns and ill-treatment of migrants, punish the perpetrators, where appropriate, and provide compensation to victims
